title: Equipment Inspection Regime (Pre-Start, Daily, LOTO)
body: Every serious equipment incident at ADW traces back to one of three checks getting skipped or rubber-stamped: pre-start, daily inspection, or LOTO. Skip pre-start and a defect that should've been caught in the yard shows up mid-shift on an active face. Skip LOTO and you've got stored energy on a machine someone thinks is dead.
keyPoints: Pre-start is the operator's job, every shift, before the machine leaves parking or the workshop — it catches the obvious stuff, not the developing stuff.
Daily inspection is maintenance's deeper pass — fluids, hoses, electrical, GET wear, tires. This is where slow failures get caught before they become breakdowns.

LOTO is non-negotiable for anything stopped for work: identify energy sources, notify affected people, isolate, lock/tag with a personal lock, bleed stored energy, then verify before anyone touches it. This is LSR 3 — a violation trigger, not a suggestion.
GET wear caught at daily inspection is what keeps a lost-GET event from happening in the first place — the two procedures are linked, not separate concerns.

Friday is the planned maintenance window here. If you see multiple units down on a Friday A&U tab, check the Friday plan before assuming unplanned breakdown — it's usually scheduled, not a fleet health problem.
apply: If a unit shows a pre-start defect that also shows up as a defect trend in daily inspections, that's your leading indicator a specific machine needs deeper attention before it becomes a breakdown line item.
